en.explanation:

$$\therefore$$ 1 মোল +n আয়ন কর্তৃক বাহিত চার্জ n Farade বা 96500 n কুলম্ব। সুতরাং 1 মিলি মোল Mn+আয়ন কর্তৃক বাহিত চার্জ 96500n $$\times$$ 10$$-$$3 কুলম্ব = n $$\times$$ 96.5 কুলম্ব।

$$\therefore$$ n = 193/96.5 = 2

$$\therefore$$ n এর মান 2।

Consider the following two first order reactions occurring at 298 K with same initial concentration of A :

(1) A $$\to$$ B; rate constant, k = 0.693 min$$-$$1

(2) A $$\to$$ C; half-life, t1/2 = 0.693 min

Choose the correct option.

en.explanation:
Given, for two first order reactions.

A $$\to$$ B, k = 0.693 min$$-$$1 .... (1) and

A $$\to$$ C, t1/2 = 0.693 min ..... (2)

For first order reaction

$${t_{1/2}} = {{0.693} \over k}$$,

Thus, for the reaction A $$\to$$ B

$${t_{1/2}} = {{0.693} \over k} = {{0.693} \over {0.693}} = 1.0$$ min

Also, for first order reaction, lower the t1/2 value, faster is the reaction.

$$\because$$ $${t_{1/2}} \propto {1 \over k}$$

and k for A $$\to$$ C is $${{0.693} \over {0.693}} = 1$$ min$$-$$1

Thus, reaction (2) is faster than reaction (1) or reaction (1) is slower than reaction (2).

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

(ii) Entropy change, i.e. $$\Delta$$S is the measurement of randomness. It increases in vapour state,

i.e. $$\Delta$$S = (+) ve or $$\Delta$$S > 0

(iii) When liquid H2O changes into vapour H2O, it requires heat energy. Thus, $$\Delta$$H > 0

$$ \therefore $$ y = 0

$$ \Rightarrow {x^2} - (p + {x_1})x + p{x_1} + q{y_1} = 0$$

Also, the discriminant of above equation will be equal to zero because circle touches X-axis.

$$ \therefore $$ $${(p + {x_1})^2} = 4(p{x_1} + q{y_1})$$

$$ \Rightarrow {p^2} + x_1^2 + 2p{x_1} = 4p{x_1} + 4q{y_1}$$

$$ \Rightarrow x_1^2 - 2p{x_1} + {p^2} = 4q{y_1}$$

$$ \Rightarrow {({x_1} - p)^2} = 4q{y_1}$$

Therefore, the locus of point B is

$${(x - p)^2} = 4qy$$

en.explanation:

We have,

$$f(a) = f(b) = 0$$

$$ \Rightarrow h(a) = f'(a) + f(a)g'(a) = f'(a)$$

and $$h(b) = f'(b) + f(b)g'(b) = f'(b)$$

$$ \therefore $$ $$h(a)\,.\,h(b) = f'(a)\,.\,f'(b) < 0$$

Again, let $$m(x) = g'(x) + kg(x)$$

$$ \Rightarrow m(a) = g'(a) + kg(a) = g'(a)$$

$$ \Rightarrow m(b) = g'(b) + kg(b) = g'(b)$$

$$ \therefore $$ $$m(a)\,.\,m(b) = g'(a)\,.\,g'(b) < 0$$

$$ \therefore $$ m(x) = 0 has root between (a, b).

So, option (a) and (c) are correct.

A ray of light is reflected by a plane mirror. $${\widehat e_0}$$, $$\widehat e$$ and $$\widehat n$$ be the unit vectors along the incident ray, reflected ray and the normal to the reflecting surface respectively.

Which of the following gives an expression for $$\widehat e$$?
en.explanation:
According to the question,


We know that incident ray, reflected ray and normal lie in the same plane.

and angle of incidence = angle of reflection

Therefore, $$\widehat n$$ will be along the angle bisector of $$\widehat e$$ and $$-$$$$\widehat e$$0,

i.e. $$\widehat n = {{\widehat e + ( - {{\widehat e}_0})} \over {|\widehat e - {{\widehat e}_0}|}}$$ ... (i)

[$$ \because $$ Bisector will along a vector dividing in same ratio as the ratio of sides forming that angle]

But $$\widehat n$$ is a unit vector where $$|\widehat e - {\widehat e_0}| = OC$$

$$ = 2OP = 2|\widehat e|$$

$$\cos \theta = 2\cos \theta $$

Substituting this value in Eq. (i) , we get

$$\widehat n = {{\widehat e - {{\widehat e}_0}} \over {2\cos \theta }}$$

$$\widehat e = {\widehat e_0} + (2\cos \theta )\widehat n$$

$$\widehat e = {\widehat e_0} - 2(\widehat n\,.\,{\widehat e_0})\widehat n$$ [$$ \because $$ $$\widehat n\,.\,{\widehat e_0} = - \cos \theta $$]

bn.content: একটি আলোকরশ্মি একটি সমতল দর্পণে প্রতিফলিত হল। $${\widehat e_0}$$, $$\widehat e$$ এবং $$\widehat n$$ যথাক্রমে আপতিত রশ্মি, প্রতিফলিত রশ্মি এবং প্রতিফলক তলের উপর অভিলম্বের অভিমুখে একক ভেক্টর। তাহলে $$\widehat e$$-কে নীচের কোনটির দ্বারা প্রকাশ করা যেতে পারে?
bn.explanation:
ধরি, $$\widehat e$$ ও $$\widehat n$$-এর মধ্যবর্তী কোণ = $$\theta $$

$$ \Rightarrow {\widehat e_0}\,.\,\widehat n = 1.1.\cos \theta = \cos \theta $$

$$\therefore$$ $${\widehat e_0}$$ ও $$\widehat n$$-এর মধ্যবর্তী কোণ $$ = (180 - \theta )$$

$$ \Rightarrow {\widehat e_0}\,.\,\widehat n = 1.1.\cos (180 - \theta ) = - \cos \theta $$

এখন, $$\widehat e\,.\,\widehat n - {\widehat e_0}\,.\,\widehat n = \cos \theta - ( - \cos \theta ) = 2\cos \theta $$

$$ \Rightarrow (\widehat e - {\widehat e_0})\,.\,\widehat n = 2( - {\widehat e_0}\,.\,\widehat n)$$

$$ \Rightarrow (\widehat e - {\widehat e_0})\,.\,\widehat n.\widehat n = - 2({\widehat e_0}\,.\,\widehat n)\widehat n$$

$$ \Rightarrow \widehat e - {\widehat e_0} = - 2({\widehat e_0}\,.\,\widehat n)\widehat n$$

$$ \Rightarrow \widehat e = {\widehat e_0} - 2({\widehat e_0}\,.\,\widehat n)\widehat n$$

en.content: A parent nucleus X undergoes $$\alpha$$-decay with a half-life of 75000 yrs. The daughter nucleus Y undergoes $$\beta$$-decay with a half-life of 9 months. In a particular sample, it is found that the rate of emission of $$\beta$$-particles is nearly constant (over several months) at $${10^7}/h$$. What will be the number of $$\alpha$$-particles emitted in an hour?
en.explanation:
According to the question,

$$X\buildrel {\alpha - particle} \over \longrightarrow Y\buildrel {\beta - particle} \over \longrightarrow Z(say)$$

According to Rutherford Soddy law of radioactive decay, the rate of decay of radioactive along at any instant is proportional to the number of atoms present at that instant

$${{dN} \over {dt}} = - \lambda N$$

Since, $$\lambda $$ = constant (decay constant) and N = number of atoms

Rate of decay of Y particle is given as,

$${\lambda _X}{N_X} - {\lambda _Y}{N_Y} = {{d{N_Y}} \over {dt}} = 0$$

[$$ \because $$ Decay rate for $$\beta$$-particle become constant after some time]

Given, rate of emission of $$\beta$$-particle = $${10^7}/h$$

$$ \therefore $$ $${\lambda _X}{N_X} - {\lambda _Y}{N_Y} = {10^7}/h$$

en.content: A proton and an electron initially at rest are accelerated by the same potential difference. Assuming that a proton is 2000 times heavier than an electron, what will be the relation between the de Broglie wavelength of the proton ($$\lambda$$<sub>p</sub>) and that of electron ($$\lambda$$<sub>e</sub>)?
en.explanation:
As we know that de-Broglie wavelength is given as $$\lambda = {h \over p} = {h \over {mv}}$$ ....(i)

where, h = Plank constant

p = momentum of particle

v = velocity of particle

and m = mass of the particle.

Eq. (i) can be written as,

$$\lambda = {h \over {2m(KE)}} = {h \over {\sqrt {2mqv} }}$$ [$$ \because $$ KE = qv]

where, KE = Kinetic energy of particle

Hence, $$\lambda \propto {1 \over {\sqrt m }}$$

Now, $${{{\lambda _{proton}}} \over {{\lambda _{electron}}}} = \sqrt {{{{m_{electron}}} \over {{m_{proton}}}}} $$

Given, mass of proton, $${m_{proton}} = 2000{m_{electron}}$$

$${{{\lambda _{proton}}} \over {{\lambda _{electron}}}} = \sqrt {{1 \over {2000}}} $$

$${{{\lambda _{proton}}} \over {{\lambda _{electron}}}} = {1 \over {20\sqrt 5 }} \Rightarrow {\lambda _p} = {{{\lambda _e}} \over {20\sqrt 5 }}$$

bn.explanation:
$$\lambda = {h \over {\sqrt {2mqV} }}$$

$$\therefore$$ $${\lambda _p} = {h \over {\sqrt {2{m_p}eV} }}$$ এবং $${\lambda _e} = {h \over {\sqrt {2{m_e}eV} }}$$

$$\therefore$$ $${{{\lambda _p}} \over {{\lambda _e}}} = \sqrt {{{{m_e}} \over {{m_p}}}} = {1 \over {2000}} = {1 \over {20\sqrt 5 }}$$

$$\therefore$$ $${\lambda _p} = {{{\lambda _e}} \over {20\sqrt 5 }}$$

en.content: To which of the following the angular velocity of the electron in the n-th Bohr orbit is proportional?
en.explanation:
According to the Bohr's atomic model,

Angular momentum, $$L = mvr = {{nh} \over {2\pi }}$$ .... (i)

Since, angular velocity $$\omega = {v \over r}$$

$$ \Rightarrow v = r\omega $$

From Eq. (i), we get

$$m(r\omega )r = {{nh} \over {2\pi }}$$

$$m\omega {r^2} = {{nh} \over {2\pi }}$$

$$\omega = {{nh} \over {2\pi m{r^2}}}$$ .... (ii)

Since, the radius of the electron in nth orbit of Bohr's atomic model is given as, $$r = {{{n^2}{h^2}{\varepsilon _o}} \over {\pi mz{e^2}}}$$ .... (iii)

Squaring the Eq. (iii) and substituting its value in Eq. (ii), we get,

$$\omega = {{nh{{(\pi mze)}^2}} \over {2\pi m({n^4}{h^4}\varepsilon _0^2)}} \Rightarrow \omega \propto {1 \over {{n^3}}}$$

en.content: The density of the material of a cube can be estimated by measuring its mass and the length of one of its sides. If the maximum error in the measurement of mass and length are 0.3% and 0.2% respectively, the maximum error in the estimation of the density of the cube is approximately
en.explanation:
Given,

Maximum error in the measurement of mass = 0.3% Maximum error in the measurement of length = 0.2%

We known that,

Error in density is given as,

Density, $$\rho = {{mass(m)} \over {volume(v)}} = {m \over {{L^3}}}$$

where, L = side of cube

Error in density is given as,

$$\left( {{{\Delta \rho } \over \rho }} \right) = {{\Delta m} \over m} + {{3\Delta L} \over L}$$

or $$\left( {{{\Delta \rho } \over \rho }} \right) \times 100 = \left( {{{\Delta m} \over m} + {{3\Delta L} \over L}} \right) \times 100$$

Substituting the given values, we get

$${\left( {{{\Delta \rho } \over \rho }} \right)_{\max }} = (0.3\% + 3(0.2)\% ) = 0.3\% + 0.6\% $$

$$ \therefore $$ Maximum percentage error measurement of density $${\left( {{{\Delta \rho } \over \rho }} \right)_{\max }} = 0.9\% $$

en.content: Two particles are simultaneously projected in the horizontal direction from a point P at a certain height. The initial velocities of the particles are oppositely directed to each other and have magnitude v each. The separation between the particles at a time when their position vectors (drawn from the point P) are mutually perpendicular, is
en.explanation:
According to the question,


In two dimension, the position vectors r1 and r2 represented as

$${r_1} = vt\widehat i - {1 \over 2}g{t^2}\widehat j$$ ...(i)

$${r_2} = vt( - \widehat i) - {1 \over 2}g{t^2}(\widehat j)$$ ... (ii)

$$ \because $$ we know that, when the two vectors are mutually perpendicular, i.e.

$$\theta = 90^\circ $$

So, $${r_1}\,.\,{r_2} = {r_1}{r_2}\cos 90^\circ $$

$${r_1}\,.\,{r_2} = 0$$

Substituting the values r1 and r2 in the above relation, we get

$$((vt)\widehat i - {1 \over 2}g{t^2}\widehat j)\,.\,(vt( - \widehat i) - {1 \over 2}g{t^2}(\widehat j)) = 0$$

$$ - {v^2}{t^2} + {1 \over 4}4{g^2}{t^4} = 0$$ (where, $$\widehat i\,.\,\widehat i = \widehat j\,.\,\widehat j = \widehat k\,.\,\widehat k = 1$$)

$${v^2}{t^2} = {1 \over 4}{g^2}{t^4}$$

$$ \Rightarrow {v^2} = {1 \over 4}{g^2}{t^2}$$

$$ \therefore $$ Magnitude of velocity of the particles, $$v = {1 \over 2}gt$$

We know that, separation distance between particles at a time t

$$\Delta x = 2vt$$

bn.content: নির্দিষ্ট উচ্চতার কোন একটি বিন্দু P থেকে দুটি কণাকে একইসঙ্গে অনুভূমিক অভিমুখে উৎক্ষেপ করা হল। কণা দুটির প্রাথমিক বেগের অভিমুখ একে অন্যের বিপরীতে এবং প্রত্যেকের প্রাথমিক বেগের মান v । যে মুহূর্তে কণা দুটির স্থান ভেক্টর (P বিন্দু থেকে অঙ্কিত) পরস্পরের উপর লম্ব হয়, তখন তাদের মধ্যেকার দূরত্ব হয় -
bn.explanation:

$$\overrightarrow {{r_1}} = vt\,\widehat i + {1 \over 2}g{t^2}( - \widehat j)$$

$$\overrightarrow {{r_2}} = vt( - \,\widehat i) + {1 \over 2}g{t^2}( - \widehat j)$$

এখন, $$\overrightarrow {{r_1}} $$ ও $$\overrightarrow {{r_2}} $$ পরস্পর লম্ব হওয়ায়, $$\overrightarrow {{r_1}} \,.\,\overrightarrow {{r_2}} = 0$$

$$ \Rightarrow - {v^2}{t^2} + {1 \over 4}{g^2}{t^4} = 0$$

$$ \Rightarrow {v^2} = {1 \over 4}{g^2}{t^2}$$

$$ \Rightarrow v = {1 \over 2}gt \Rightarrow t = {{2v} \over g}$$

$$\therefore$$ তাদের মধ্যকার দূরত্ব $$\Delta x = \Delta {x_1} + \Delta {x_2} = vt + vt = 2vt = 2v\,.\,{{2v} \over g}$$

$$ \Rightarrow \Delta x = {{4{v^2}} \over g}$$

en.content:
A compressive force is applied to a uniform rod of rectangular cross-section so that its length decreases by 1%. If the Poisson's ratio for the material of the rod be 0.2, which of the following statements is correct?

"The volume approximately ................."
en.explanation:
Given, decrement in the length = 1%

Poisson's ratio for material of the rod, $$\sigma$$ = 0.2

As we know that,

Volume = v = $$\pi$$r2l, [where, l is the length of the rod]

$${{\Delta V} \over V} = {{2\Delta r} \over r} + {{\Delta l} \over l}$$ ...(i)

Since, Poisson's ratio, $$\sigma = {{ - \Delta D/D} \over {\Delta L/L}}$$

$$ = {{ - \Delta r/r} \over {\Delta L/L}}$$

So, Eq. (i) can be written as,

$${{\Delta V} \over V} = {{\Delta l} \over l}(1 - 2\sigma )$$

$${{\Delta V} \over V} \times 100 = \left( {{{\Delta l} \over l} \times 100} \right) \times (1 - 2\sigma )$$

$$ = - 1 \times [1 - 2 \times (0.2)]$$

$$ = - 1 \times [1 - 0.4]$$

$$ = - 0.6\% $$

Here, negative sign shows the decrement in the volume.

এখন, পয়সন অনুপাত $$(\sigma ) = {{ - {{\Delta a} \over a}} \over {{{\Delta l} \over l}}} = {{ - {{\Delta b} \over b}} \over {{{\Delta l} \over l}}} \Rightarrow {{\Delta a} \over a} = - \sigma {{\Delta l} \over l}$$

en.content: Two black bodies A and B have equal surface areas are maintained at temperatures 27$$^\circ$$C and 177$$^\circ$$C respectively. What will be the ratio of the thermal energy radiated per second by A to that by B?
en.explanation:
According to the question,

Area of both bodies A and B = A

Temperature of body A = 27$$^\circ$$C = 27 + 273 K

Temperature of body B = 177$$^\circ$$C = 177 + 273 K

Now, by Stefan-Boltzmann law, thermal energy radiated per second by a body

Q = $$\sigma$$AT4,

where, A = Area

T = Temperature

and $$\sigma$$ = Stefan-Boltzmann's constant

So, the ratio of thermal energy radiated per second by A that by B is

$${{{Q_1}} \over {{Q_2}}} = {{\sigma A} \over {\sigma A}}{\left( {{{{T_1}} \over {{T_2}}}} \right)^4}$$

Now, $${{{Q_1}} \over {{Q_2}}} = {\left( {{{{T_1}} \over {{T_2}}}} \right)^4}$$

$${{{Q_1}} \over {{Q_2}}} = {\left( {{{273 + 27} \over {273 + 177}}} \right)^4}$$

$${{{Q_1}} \over {{Q_2}}} = {\left( {{{300} \over {450}}} \right)^4}$$

$${{{Q_1}} \over {{Q_2}}} = {\left( {{2 \over 3}} \right)^4} = \left( {{{16} \over {81}}} \right)$$

Ratio of thermal energy radiated per second

$${Q_1}:{Q_2} = 16:81$$

bn.content: দুটি কৃষ্ণবস্তু A এবং B-এর পৃষ্ঠতলের ক্ষেত্রফল সমান এবং তাদেরকে যথাক্রমে 27$$^\circ$$C এবং 177$$^\circ$$C উষ্ণতায় রাখা হল। A এবং B থেকে প্রতি সেকেন্ডে যে তাপীয় শক্তি বিকিরিত হয় তাদের অনুপাত কত ?
bn.explanation:
কৃষ্ণবস্তু হতে প্রতি সেকেন্ডে বিকীর্ণ তাপ Q হলে, $$Q = \sigma A{T^{ 4}}$$

$$\therefore$$ $${{{Q_1}} \over {{Q_2}}} = {\left( {{{{T_1}} \over {{T_2}}}} \right)^4} = {\left( {{{273 + 27} \over {273 + 177}}} \right)^4} = {\left( {{{300} \over {450}}} \right)^4} = {\left( {{2 \over 3}} \right)^4} = {{16} \over {81}}$$

Concept :

স্টিফান - বোলজমান সূত্র (Stefan - Boltzmann law) : 1879 সালে পরীক্ষা হতে প্রাপ্ত ফলের ভিত্তিতে বলেন - কোন বস্তু হতে নির্গত মোট বিকিরণ তার পরম উষ্ণতার চতুর্থ ঘাতের সমানুপাতী। 1884 সালে বোলজমান তাপগতিবিদ্যার সাহায্যে সূত্রের তাত্ত্বিক প্রমাণ দেন এবং দেখান এটি কেবল আদর্শ কৃষ্ণ বস্তুর ক্ষেত্রে প্রযোজ্য। বরতমানে সূত্রটি স্টিফান - বোলজমান সূত্র নামে পরিচিত।

সূত্র : কোন আদর্শ কৃষ্ণ বস্তুর পৃষ্ঠের একক ক্ষেত্রফল হতে একক সময়ে সকল তরঙ্গ দৈর্ঘ্য বিবেচনায় মোট বিকীর্ণ শক্তির পরিমাণ তার পরম উষ্ণতার চতুর্থ ঘাতের সমানুপাতী হয়।

T উষ্ণতা সম্পন্ন কোন আদর্শ কৃষ্ণ বস্তুর পৃষ্ঠের একক ক্ষেত্রফল হতে একক সময়ে বিকীর্ণ মোট শক্তি E হলে $$E \propto {T^4}$$ or, $$E = \sigma {T^4}$$ ..... (1)

যেখানে $$\sigma$$ একটি সার্বজনীন ধ্রুবক যাকে স্টিফান - বোলজমান ধ্রুবক বা স্টিফানের ধ্রুবক বলে।

স্পষ্টতই বস্তুটি পারিপার্শ্বিক হতে কিছু বিকিরণ শোষণও করে। ধরা যাক T উষ্ণতার আদর্শ কৃষ্ণ বস্তু T0 উষ্ণতার একটি আদর্শ কৃষ্ণ বস্তুর (পারিপার্শ্বিক) মধ্যে রাখা আছে। বস্তুটির পৃষ্ঠের ক্ষেত্রফল A হলে তার সমগ্র পৃষ্ঠ হতে মোট বিকিরণ হার $$u = \sigma A{T^4}$$ । বস্তুটি পারিপার্শ্বিকের সহিত তাপীয় সাম্যে থাকলে তার বিকিরণ নির্গমন হার পারিপার্শ্বিক হতে বিকিরণ শোষণ হারের সমান হতো। সুতরাং পারিপার্শ্বিক হতে বিকিরণ শোষণ হার $${u_0} = \sigma AT_0^4$$

সুতরাং বস্তুতিএ বিকিরণ প্রক্রিয়ায় লব্ধ তাপ ক্ষয়ের হার,

$$\Delta u = \sigma A{T^4} - \sigma AT_0^4$$

or, $$\Delta u = \sigma A({T^4} - T_0^4)$$ ....... (2)

আলোচ্য বস্তুটি আদর্শ কৃষ্ণ বস্তু না হলে তার বিকিরণ হার (1) নং সমীকরণ হতে প্রাপ্ত মান অপেক্ষা কম হয় তবে তা উষ্ণতার চতুর্থ ঘাতের সমানুপাতীই থাকে। সেক্ষেত্রে বস্তুর একক ক্ষেত্রফল হতে একক সময়ে বিকীর্ণ শক্তির পরিমাণ $$E = \in \sigma {T^4}$$ ...... (3)

যেখানে $$\in$$ একটি ধ্রুবক যার মান বস্তুর পৃষ্ঠ তলের প্রকৃতির উপর নির্ভরশীল এবং $$1 \le \in \le 0$$ হয়। $$\in$$ কে তলের আপেক্ষিক বিকিরণ ক্ষমতা (emissivity) বলে। এরমান আদর্শ সাদা বস্তুর (পূর্ণ প্রতিফলক) ক্ষেত্রে 0 ও আদর্শ কৃষ্ণ বস্তুর ক্ষেত্রে 1 হয়।

en.content: What will be the molar specific heat at constant volume of an ideal gas consisting of rigid diatomic molecules?
en.explanation:
For a gas at temperature T, the internal energy,

$$U = {f \over 2}\mu RT$$

where, f = degree of freedom

$$ \Rightarrow $$ Change in energy, $$\Delta U = {f \over 2}\mu R\Delta T$$ .... (i)

Also, as we know for any gas heat supplied at constant volume

$$(\Delta {Q_v}) = \mu {C_v}\Delta T = \Delta U$$ .... (ii)

where, Cv = molar specific heat at constant volume

From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get

$${C_v} = {1 \over 2}fR$$

For diatomic gas, degree of freedom, f = 5

$${C_v} = {5 \over 2}R$$

en.content: Five identical capacitors, of capacitance 20$$\mu$$F each, are connected to a battery of 150V, in a combination as shown in the diagram. What is the total amount of charge stored?
en.explanation:
The given circuit shows a balanced Wheatstone bridge. Now, the circuit becomes


In the branch AB, both capacitor are arranged in the series combination. Hence, its equivalent capacitance is given by

$${1 \over {{C_{AB}}}} = {1 \over {20}} + {1 \over {20}} = {2 \over {20}} = {1 \over {10}}$$

$${C_{AB}} = 10\mu F$$

Similarly, in branch CD,

$${C_{CD}} = 10\mu F$$

Now, CAB and CCD are connected in parallel combination. Hence, the equivalent capacitance of the circuit,

$${C_{eq}} = 10 + 10 = 20\mu F$$

We know that, charge $$Q = {C_{eq}}V$$

$$Q = 20 \times {10^{ - 6}} \times 150V$$

Amount of charge stored $$Q = 3 \times {10^{ - 3}}C$$

en.content: When a 60 mH inductor and a resistor are connected in series with an AC voltage source, the voltage leads the current by 60$$^\circ$$. If the inductor is replaced by a 0.5 $$\mu$$F capacitor, the voltage lags behind the current by 30$$^\circ$$. What is the frequency of the AC supply?
en.explanation:
Given, inductance of inductor, L = 60 mH

= 60 $$ \times $$ 10$$-$$3 H

Phase difference between voltage and current in L-R circuit, $$\theta$$1 = 60$$^\circ$$

Capacitance of capacitor, C = 0.5 $$\mu$$F = 0.5 $$ \times $$ 10$$-$$6F

Phase difference between voltage and current in R-C circuit, $$\theta$$2 = 30$$^\circ$$

For L-R circuit,

$$\tan {\theta _1} = {{{X_L}} \over R}$$

$$\tan {\theta _1} = {{\omega L} \over R}$$ .... (i) [$$ \because $$ $${X_L} = \omega L$$]

Similarly, for R-C circuit,

$$\tan {\theta _2} = {{{X_C}} \over R}$$

$$\tan {\theta _2} = {{{1 \over {\omega C}}} \over R}$$ ...(ii) $$ \because $$ $$\left[ {{X_C} = {1 \over {\omega C}}} \right]$$

From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get

$${{\tan {\theta _1}} \over {\tan {\theta _2}}} = {{\omega L} \over {R \times {1 \over {\omega CR}}}} = {\omega ^2}LC$$

$${{\tan 60^\circ } \over {\tan 30^\circ }} = {\omega ^2}LC$$

$${{\sqrt 3 } \over {1/\sqrt 3 }} = {\omega ^2}LC$$

$${\omega ^2}LC = 3$$

$${\omega ^2} = {3 \over {LC}}$$$${\omega ^2} = {3 \over {60 \times {{10}^{ - 3}} \times 0.5 \times {{10}^{ - 6}}}}$$

$${\omega ^2} = {3 \over {30 \times {{10}^{ - 9}}}}$$

$$\omega = \sqrt {{{10}^8}} $$

$$\omega = {10^4}$$

As we know that,

$$\omega = 2\pi f$$

$$f = {\omega \over {2\pi }} = {{{{10}^4}} \over {2\pi }}Hz = {1 \over {2\pi }} \times {10^4}Hz$$

en.content: When the frequency of the light used is changed from $$4 \times {10^{14}}{s^{ - 1}}$$ to $$5 \times {10^{14}}{s^{ - 1}}$$, the angular width of the principal (central) maximum in a single slit Fraunhoffer diffraction pattern changes by 0.6 radian. What is the width of the slit (assume that the experiment is performed in vacuum)?
en.explanation:
Given, initial frequency of light,

$${f_1} = 4 \times {10^{14}}{s^{ - 1}}$$

Final frequency of light, $${f_2} = 5 \times {10^{14}}{s^{ - 1}}$$

Change in wavelength, $$\Delta \lambda = {\lambda _1} - {\lambda _2}$$

or $$\Delta \lambda = {c \over {{f_1}}} - {c \over {{f_2}}}$$

$$ = {{3 \times {{10}^8}} \over {4 \times {{10}^{14}}}} - {{3 \times {{10}^8}} \over {5 \times {{10}^{14}}}}$$

$$ = {{3 \times {{10}^8}} \over {{{10}^{14}}}}\left( {{1 \over 4} - {1 \over 5}} \right)$$

$$ = {{3 \times {{10}^8}} \over {{{10}^{14}}}} \times {1 \over {20}}$$

$$ = 1.5 \times {10^{ - 7}}$$ m

Now, we know that,

Angular width of central maxima,

$$\theta = {{2\lambda } \over d}$$ or $$\Delta \theta = {{2\Delta \lambda } \over d}$$

$$d = {{2\Delta \lambda } \over {\Delta \theta }}$$

Here, $$\Delta \theta $$ = 0.6 radian

$$d = {{2 \times 1.5 \times {{10}^{ - 7}}} \over {0.6}} = 5 \times {10^{ - 7}}$$ m

bn.content: যখন ব্যবহৃত আলোর কম্পাঙ্ক 4 $$\times$$ 1014s$$-$$1 থেকে 5 $$\times$$ 1014s$$-$$1-এ পরিবর্তন করা হয়, এক রেখাছিদ্র ফ্রনহফার অপবর্তন নকশার মুখ্য (কেন্দ্রীয়) পটির কৌণিক প্রস্থ 0.6 রেডিয়ান পরিমাণ পরিবর্তিত হয়। রেখাছিদ্রের প্রস্থ (ধরে নাও পরীক্ষাটি শূন্য মাধ্যমে সম্পন্ন হয়েছে) কত ?
bn.explanation:
আমরা জানি,

$$\theta = {{2\lambda } \over d} \Rightarrow \Delta \theta = {{2\Delta \lambda } \over d} \Rightarrow d = {{2\Delta \lambda } \over {\Delta \theta }}$$

এক্ষেত্রে, $$\Delta \lambda = {C \over {{V_1}}} - {C \over {{V_2}}} = {{3 \times {{10}^8}} \over {4 \times {{10}^{14}}}} - {{3 \times {{10}^8}} \over {4 \times {{10}^{14}}}} = 1.5 \times {10^{ - 7}}$$

অতএব, $$d = {{2 \times 1.5 \times {{10}^{ - 7}}} \over {0.6}} = 5 \times {10^{ - 7}}m$$

en.content: A capacitor of capacitance C is connected in series with a resistance R and DC source of emf E through a key. The capacitor starts charging when the key is closed. By the time the capacitor has been fully charged, what amount of energy is dissipated in the resistance R?
en.explanation:
We know that, energy stored in the capacitor

= $${1 \over 2}C{E^2}$$

and energy supplied by the source of emf = CE2

$$ \therefore $$ Energy dissipated in resistance R

= Energy supplied by the source of emf E $$-$$ Energy stored in the capacitor

= $$C{E^2} - {1 \over 2}C{E^2}$$

$$ = \left( {1 - {1 \over 2}} \right)C{E^2} = {1 \over 2}C{E^2}$$

bn.content: C ধারকত্বের একটি ধারক, একটি রোধ R এবং E তড়িৎচালক বলের একটি সমপ্রবাহী (DC) উৎস একটি চাবির সাহায্যে শ্রেণিসমবায়ে যুক্ত করা হল। চাবিটি বন্ধ করা হলে ধারকটি আহিত হতে শুরু করে। যতক্ষণ ধরে ধারকটি সম্পূর্ণ আহিত হবে, ততক্ষণে R রোধের মধ্য দিয়ে শক্তির অবক্ষয়ের পরিমাণ কত হবে?

en.content: A horizontal fire hose with a nozzle of cross-sectional area $${5 \over {\sqrt {21} }} \times {10^{ - 3}}{m^2}$$ delivers a cubic metre of water in 10s. What will be the maximum possible increase in the temperature of water while it hits a rigid wall (neglecting the effect of gravity)?
en.explanation:
Given, cross sectional area of nozzle $$A = {5 \over {\sqrt {21} }} \times {10^{ - 3}}{m^2}$$

and rate of heat transfer $$Q = {1 \over {10}} = {10^{ - 1}}{m^3}/s$$

$$ \because $$ Heat transfer Q = AV

$$ \therefore $$ $$V = {Q \over A} = {{{{10}^{ - 1}}{m^3}/s} \over {{5 \over {\sqrt {21} }} \times {{10}^{ - 3}}{m^2}}} = 2\sqrt {21} \times 10m/s$$

When in hits a rigid wall then maximum possible increase in temperature of water can be expressed as

$${1 \over 2}m{v^2} = ms\Delta T$$ ...(i)

where, m = mass, s = specific heat of water = 1 cal / g = 4.2 $$ \times $$ 103 J / kg and $$\Delta T$$ = increase in temperature

From Eq. (i), $$\Delta T = {1 \over 2}{{{v^2}} \over s}$$

$$ = {{{{(2\sqrt {21} \times {{10}^1})}^2}} \over {2 \times 4.2 \times {{10}^3}}}$$

$$ = {{84 \times {{10}^2}} \over {8.4 \times {{10}^3}}}$$

= $$1^\circ $$C

bn.content: একটি অনুভূমিক অগ্নিনির্বাপক হোসপাইপ-এর $${5 \over {\sqrt {21} }} \times {10^{ - 3}}$$m2 ক্ষেত্রফল বিশিষ্ট সরুমুখ (nozzle) থেকে 10 সেকেন্ডে 1 ঘনমিটার জল নির্গত হয়। যখন ওই জল একটি দৃঢ় দেয়ালে আঘাত করে তখন তার সর্বাধিক সম্ভাব্য উষ্ণতা-বৃদ্ধি (অভিকর্ষের প্রভাব উপেক্ষণীয়) কত হবে ?

en.content: Two identical blocks of ice move in opposite directions with equal speed and collide with each other. What will be the minimum speed required to make both the blocks melt completely, if the initial temperatures of the blocks were $$-$$8$$^\circ$$C each? (Specific heat of ice is 2100 Jkg<sup>$$-$$1</sup>K<sup>$$-$$1</sup> and latent heat of fusion of ice is 3.36 $$ \times $$ 10<sup>5</sup> Jkg<sup>$$-$$1</sup>)
en.explanation:
Maximum loss in K.E. = Total K.E. energy before collision of two ice blocks

$$K.E{._{\max \,loss}} = {1 \over 2}m{v^2} + {1 \over 2}m{v^2} = m{v^2}$$

This maximum loss in kinetic energy will be equal to loss in heat to melt two ice block.

$$ \Rightarrow m{v^2} = (ms\Delta \theta + mL)2$$ .... (i)

According to question,

$$L = 3.36 \times {10^5}J\,k{g^{ - 1}}$$

$$S = 2100J\,k{g^{ - 1}}{K^{ - 1}}$$

$$\Delta \theta = 8^\circ C$$

From Eq. (i) $$v = \sqrt {2(s\Delta \theta + L)} $$

$$ = \sqrt {2(2100 \times 8 + 3.36 \times {{10}^5})} $$

$$v = 840\,m{s^{ - 1}}$$

bn.content:
বরফের দুটি অনুরূপ ব্লক পরস্পরের বিপরীত অভিমুখে সমান দ্রুতিতে চলমান হয় এবং একে অন্যকে ধাক্কা দেয়। যদি ব্লক দুটির প্রত্যেকটির প্রাথমিক উষ্ণতা $$-$$8$$^\circ$$C হয় তবে ব্লক দুটির সম্পূর্ণ গলনের জন্য প্রয়োজনীয় সর্বনিম্ন দ্রুতি কত হবে ?

(বরফের আপেক্ষিক তাপ হল 2100 Jkg$$-$$1K$$-$$1 এবং বরফ গলনের লীনতাপ হল 3.36 $$\times$$ 105 Jkg$$-$$1)
bn.explanation:
$${(K.E)_{\max }} = {1 \over 2}.\mu .{v^2} = {1 \over 2}.\left( {{m \over 2}} \right){(2u)^2} = m{u^2}$$

এখন, $$m{u^2} = 2(ms\Delta \theta + mL)$$

$$ \Rightarrow {u^2} = 2(s\Delta \theta + L)$$

$$ \Rightarrow u = \sqrt {2(2100 \times 8 + 336000)} $$

$$ = 840$$ m/s

en.content: A particle with charge q moves with a velocity v in a direction perpendicular to the directions of uniform electric and magnetic fields, E and B respectively, which are mutually perpendicular to each other. Which one of the following gives the condition for which the particle moves undeflected in its original trajectory?
en.explanation:
According to the question,

Charge on particle is = q

Velocity of particle = v

Due to uniform electric field,

electric force on particle

Felectric = qE ....(i)

Due to a uniform magnetic field,

,magnetic force on particle is given by,

Fmagnetic = q(v $$ \times $$ B) ....(ii)

When v is perpendicular to E and B, which are mutually perpendicular to each other,

Felectric = Fmagnetic

From Eqs. (i) and (ii)

qE = qvB

$$ \therefore $$ $$v = {E \over B}$$

So, $$v = {E \over B}$$ is the condition for which the particle moves undeflected in its original trajectory.

bn.content: পরস্পর লম্ব-অভিমুখী সুষম তড়িৎ ও চৌম্বকক্ষেত্র, যথাক্রমে E ও B-এর সঙ্গে লম্ব অভিমুখে v বেগ নিয়ে q আধানের একটি কণা গতিশীল হল। নীচের কোন শর্তে কণাটি তার প্রারম্ভিক গতিপথ থেকে বিচ্যুত না হয়ে চলতে থাকবে ?

$$ \Rightarrow v = {E \over B}$$

en.content: A parallel plate capacitor in series with a resistance of 100$$\Omega $$, an inductor of 20 mH and an AC voltage source of variable frequency shows resonance at a frequency of $${{1250} \over \pi }$$ Hz. If this capacitor is charged by a DC voltage source to a voltage 25 V, what amount of charge will be stored in each plate of the capacitor?
en.explanation:
In given, Series R - L - C circuit

Resistance R = 100$$\Omega $$

Inductance of Inductor, L = 20 mH = 20 $$ \times $$ 10$$-$$3 H

Resonance frequency f = $${{1250} \over \pi }$$ Hz

Source voltage VDC = 25V

According to resonant frequency,

$${\omega _0} = 2\pi {f_0} = {1 \over {\sqrt {LC} }}$$

or $${(2\pi {f_0})^2} = {1 \over {LC}}$$

or $$4{\pi ^2}{{1250 \times 1250} \over {\pi \times \pi }} = {1 \over {LC}}$$

or $$C = {{1000} \over {1250 \times 1250 \times 4 \times 20}}$$ ($$ \because $$ By substituting L = 20 $$ \times $$ 10$$-$$3)

or $$C = 8 \times {10^{ - 6}}$$F

We know that, Charge $${Q_s} = CV$$

$${Q_s} = 8 \times {10^{ - 6}} \times 25 = 0.2$$ mC

So, the amount of charge stored in each plate of capacitor is 0.2 mC.

bn.content: একটি সমান্তরাল পাত ধারক, একটি 100$$\Omega$$ রোধ ও 20 mH আবেশক পরিবর্তনশীল কম্পাঙ্কের একটি পরিবর্তী (AC) ভোল্টেজ উৎসের সঙ্গে শ্রেণি সমবায়ে যুক্ত এবং ওই সমবায়ের অনুনাদী কম্পাঙ্ক $${{1250} \over \pi }Hz$$ । ওই ধারকটিকে একটি সমপ্রবাহী (DC) ভোল্টেজ উৎস দিয়ে 25 V বিভবপ্রভেদে আহিত করা হলে ধারকের প্রতি পাতে কত আধান সঞ্চিত হবে ?

en.content: Electrons are emitted with kinetic energy T from a metal plate by an irradiation of light of intensity J and frequency v. Then, which of the following will be true?
en.explanation:
In photoelectric effect, if the incident light had a frequency less than a minimum frequency v0, then no electrons are ejected regardless of the light's amplitude. This minimum frequency is also called the threshold frequency, and the value of v0 depends on the metal. For frequency greater than v0, electrons would be ejected from the metal. Furthermore, the kinetic energy of the photoelectrons is proportional to the light frequency (v).

The relationship between photoelectron kinetic energy T and light frequency v is shown in graph below


Graph shows that kinetic energy T is linearly increasing with light frequency (v). However, for a given photosensitive material and frequency of incident light, number of photoelectrons emitted per second is directly proportional to the intensity of incident light i.e., Number of electrons emitted $$ \propto $$ J.

Also, photoelectric emission is an instantaneous process.

en.content: The initial pressure and volume of a given mass of an ideal gas with $$\left( {{{{C_p}} \over {{C_V}}} = \gamma } \right)$$, taken in a cylinder fitted with a piston, are p<sub>0</sub> and V<sub>0</sub> respectively. At this stage the gas has the same temperature as that of the surrounding medium which is T<sub>0</sub>. It is adiabatically compressed to a volume equal to $${{{V_0}} \over 2}$$. Subsequently the gas is allowed to come to thermal equilibrium with the surroundings. What is the heat released to the surrounding?
en.explanation:
The equation of state for an ideal gas undergoing adiabatic process is given as,

TV$$\gamma $$$$-$$1 = constant

Let the temperature after adiabatic compression as given in the question be T then,

$${T_0}{V^{\gamma - 1}} = T{\left( {{{{V_0}} \over 2}} \right)^{\gamma - 1}}$$

$$ \Rightarrow T = {T_0}{2^{\gamma - 1}}$$

Now, heat released at volume $${{{V_0}} \over 2}$$ to achieve temperature $${T_0}$$.

The net heat released can be determined by the equation,

$$\Delta Q = \mu {C_V}\Delta T$$

$$ = \mu \times {R \over {\gamma - 1}}$$ $$({T_0}{2^{\gamma - 1}} - {T_0})$$

$$ = {{\mu R{T_0}} \over {\gamma - 1}}({2^{\gamma - 1}} = 1)$$ $$ \because $$ $$(\mu {T_0}R = {p_0}{V_0})$$

$$ \therefore $$ Heat released = $${{{p_0}V} \over {\gamma - 1}}({2^{\gamma - 1}} - 1)$$

bn.content: পিস্টন যুক্ত একটি চোঙে প্রদত্ত ভরের একটি আদর্শ গ্যাসের (যেখানে $${{{C_p}} \over {{C_v}}} = \gamma $$) প্রাথমিক চাপ ও আয়তন যথাক্রমে P0 এবং V0। এই অবস্থায় গ্যাসের উষ্ণতা পারিপার্শ্বিক উষ্ণতা T0 এর সমান। একে তাপনিরুদ্ধভাবে $${{{V_0}} \over 2}$$ আয়তনে সংনমিত করা হল। তারপর গ্যাসটিকে পরিপার্শ্বের সঙ্গে সাম্যাবস্থায় আসতে দেওয়া হল। কত পরিমাণ তাপ পরিপার্শ্বে নির্গত হবে ?
bn.explanation:
যেহেতু রুদ্ধতাপ প্রক্রিয়া

$$\therefore$$ $${T_0}V_0^{\gamma - 1} = T{V^{\gamma - 1}} = T{\left( {{{{V_0}} \over 2}} \right)^{\gamma - 1}}$$

$$ \Rightarrow T = {T_0}{2^{\gamma - 1}}$$

সংনমনের পরে,

$$\Delta Q = n{C_v}.\,\Delta T = n.\,{R \over {\gamma - 1}}({T_0} - {T_0}{2^{\gamma - 1}}) = {{nR{T_0}} \over {\gamma - 1}}(1 - {2^{\gamma - 1}})$$

$$ \Rightarrow \Delta Q = {{{P_0}{V_0}} \over {\gamma - 1}}(1 - {2^{\gamma - 1}})$$

en.content: A projectile thrown with an initial velocity of 10 ms<sup>$$-$$1</sup> at an angle $$\alpha$$ with the horizontal, has a range of 5 m. Taking g = 10 ms<sup>$$-$$2</sup> and neglecting air resistance, what will be the estimated value of $$\alpha$$?
en.explanation:
Given, initial velocity of particle, u = 10 ms$$-$$1

Range, R = 5 m

Gravitational acceleration, g = 10 ms$$-$$2

As we known that,

Range of projectile, $$R = {{{u^2}\sin 2\theta } \over g}$$

$$5 = {{{{(10)}^2}\sin 2\alpha } \over {10}}$$

$$\sin 2\alpha = {5 \over {10}}$$

$$\sin 2\alpha = {1 \over 2}$$

$$\alpha = 15^\circ $$

or $$(90^\circ - 15^\circ = 75^\circ )$$

bn.content: একটি প্রাসকে 10 ms$$-$$1 প্রাথমিক বেগে অনুভূমিকের সঙ্গে $$\alpha$$ কোণে উৎক্ষেপণ করা হল যার পাল্লা 5 m । g = 10 ms$$-$$2 ধরলে এবং বাতাসের বাধা উপেক্ষা করলে $$\alpha$$-এর নির্ণীত মান কত হবে ?
